## Report: Olive Oil Consumption and Stroke Risk

**Conclusion:** The claim that consuming more olive oil reduces stroke risk is **well-supported by observational evidence and one major randomized trial**, though some caveats apply.

### Key Evidence

1. **Meta-analysis of cohort studies:** A meta-analysis found that for every 25 g/day increase in olive oil consumption, stroke risk was 26% lower (RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.60–0.92), a statistically significant association. ([Olivea](https://www.myolivea.com/blogs/research/olive-oil-stroke-cardiovascular-meta-analysis-2014))

2. **PREDIMED randomized controlled trial:** This landmark RCT (7,447 participants at high cardiovascular risk) found that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil reduced major cardiovascular events—including stroke—by approximately 30% versus a low-fat diet. Stroke specifically was reduced by about 33% in the olive oil group. ([IQ Healthspan](https://iqhealthspan.com/articles/the-mediterranean-diet-for-longevity-what-the-strongest-evidence-in-nutrition-sc); [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29897866/))

3. **Systematic review conclusion:** Olive oil is associated with lower risk of CVD and stroke, with maximum benefit at 20–30 g/day, and a potentially stronger effect for virgin olive oil. ([University of Granada](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/72282/1-s2.0-S0261561421005033-main.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y))

### Important Caveats

- **PREDIMED retraction:** The trial was retracted and republished in 2018 due to randomization irregularities. However, the reanalysis preserved the headline findings. ([Harvard Nutrition Source](https://nutritionsource.hsph.harvard.edu/2018/06/22/predimed-retraction-republication/); [BMJ](https://www.bmj.com/content/364/bmj.l341))
- **Observational confounding:** Observational studies cannot fully eliminate confounding variables; researchers have called for more study. ([Khaleej Times](https://www.khaleejtimes.com/lifestyle/health/olive-oil-lovers-have-lower-stroke-risk))

Overall, the evidence consistently points toward a protective association, but the strongest trial evidence has known methodological limitations.
